synopsis: The booklet reports UK designation of the EN 474:2022 earth-moving machinery family in August 2026 as a presumption-of-conformity route, not an automatic-braking performance matrix; however, the cited 8 August notice number 0139/26 was not confirmed on gov.uk [f2718, f2220, f2221, f2222, f2875]. No UK collision-avoidance mandate or dedicated off-road rule requiring an ML-based collision-avoidance function to meet a specified ML validation standard by 2028 was found; the mandate finding is explicitly an expert-opinion planning caution, and the review did not verify the Quarries Regulations 1999 or named industry guidance [f2227, f2393, f2225, f2226]. British guidance attributes nearly a quarter of workplace-transport deaths to reversing and 40% of quarry accidents and 60% of quarry deaths to transport, while the booklet warns that differing machine and site populations explain contrasting forward-versus-reversing accident patterns [f2994, f11493, f3618]. For on-road virtual validation, the UK's January 2024 GRVA-18-55 submission challenged the credibility of proposed R152 provisions and called for physical testing evidenced for every toolchain component, rather than only the final toolchain [f7689, f7690]. The UK CCAV-funded Sim4CAMSens program ran from 2023 to 2025 [f4767]. Other UK-origin planning and assurance references include ALARP's reasonably-practicable risk-reduction duty, Def Stan 00-56 Issue 7 safety cases for UK defence systems, and PRINCE2 seventh edition (2023), organized around stages, roles and a project initiation document [f12141, f9709, f16421].
